advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether `jira_key` should be part of public output; if not, add it to INTERNAL_KEYS (or strip it after enrichment), else surface it consistently across show/list/search.
evidence: src/rebar/reducer/_present.py:22-27: `INTERNAL_KEYS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({ "parent_status_uuid", "last_status_env_id", })` — `jira_key` is absent, so `public_state` passes it through
src/rebar/reducer/_present.py:48: `out = {k: v for k, v in state.items() if k not in INTERNAL_KEYS}`

ABSENCE: only `search_state` (reads.py:509-516) performs the enrichment; `ready_states`/`show`/`list` do not, and the reducer default state (_state.py) has no `jira_key` key, so `jira_key` appears only in search output
src/rebar/_ids.py:28: docstring notes `data.jira_key` on CREATE/SNAPSHOT is never written — the reduced state has no jira_key otherwise
advisory.finding: search enrichment adds a new top-level `jira_key` field to reduced states that survives `public_state` (not in INTERNAL_KEYS), so `rebar search <JIRA-KEY>` output now carries a `jira_key` field that `show`/`list` output for the same ticket does not — a per-surface output-shape divergence.
scenarios: A client parsing `search` JSON output sees an extra `jira_key` key on Jira-bound tickets but never on `show`/`list` of the same ticket, breaking shape assumptions or golden-output tests

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a direct unit test for binding_jira_key_map covering inversion direction, the non-str/empty entry filter, and the setdefault first-wins tiebreak on duplicate local_ids.
evidence: src/rebar/_ids.py:130-134 `out: dict[str, str] = {}` / `for jira_key, local_id in _load_binding_reverse(...).items():` / `if isinstance(jira_key, str) and jira_key and isinstance(local_id, str) and local_id:` / `out.setdefault(local_id, jira_key)`
search_files for `binding_jira_key_map` shows only the definition (src/rebar/_ids.py:121) and the single caller (src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:509) — no test file references it (ABSENCE)
The integration test in tests/interfaces/queries/test_ws5a_search.py:76-78 writes only a single well-formed binding, never a malformed entry or a duplicate local_id
advisory.finding: The new inversion function binding_jira_key_map has documented logic — inverting reverse {jira_key -> local_id} into {local_id -> jira_key}, filtering malformed non-str entries, and setdefault first-wins on duplicate local_ids — but no test exercises it directly. Every test feeds only well-formed single-entry data (integration writes {'REB-1654': tid}; the pure units never touch _ids at all). A regression that inverted the map the wrong way, dropped the non-str filter, or changed the tiebreak would not be caught.
scenarios: A refactor that inverts the map incorrectly (jira_key <-> local_id swapped) still passes the single-entry integration test because both sides happen to round-trip through search
A future change drops the `isinstance(local_id, str)` guard; a non-str value in reverse leaks into a state's jira_key and is never caught
advisory.suggested_fix: Add tests/unit tests that call binding_jira_key_map on a tmp tracker_dir with (a) a normal multi-entry reverse asserting the exact {local_id: jira_key} inversion, (b) a reverse containing non-str/empty keys/values asserting they are dropped, and (c) two jira keys mapping to one local_id asserting the first wins.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen the bound-Jira-key integration test to assert the unbound 'noise' ticket is EXCLUDED from a Jira-key search (equality on the id set, not just membership).
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:510-516 iterates states and sets `st['jira_key'] = jira_key` only when `jira_by_ticket.get(ticket_id)` is truthy

tests/interfaces/queries/test_ws5a_search.py:70-83 creates a 'noise' ticket but asserts only `tid in _ids(...)` for the bound key, never that the noise ticket is excluded from a Jira-key search at the reads.py seam (ABSENCE)
advisory.finding: The reads.py enrichment loop's partial-enrichment behavior — only bound tickets get a jira_key while unbound tickets are left untouched — is asserted only at the pure-reducer level (test_identifier_widening_does_not_leak_into_text_haystack), not through the actual binding_jira_key_map/search_state seam. The integration test binds exactly one ticket and asserts only that it is found; it never asserts that the co-existing unbound 'noise' ticket is NOT annotated/matched by a Jira-key query at the real seam.
scenarios: A regression that annotates every state with the same (first) jira_key would make a Jira-key search return all tickets; the integration test's `assert tid in ...` (membership, not equality) would still pass
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_search_matches_bound_jira_key, capture the noise ticket id and assert `_ids(rebar.search('REB-1654')) == {tid}` (and the noise id not in the result) so over-annotation at the reads.py enrichment seam is caught.
